title: Quantile regression to examine the association of air pollution with subclinical atherosclerosis in an adolescent population.
ehr_evidence: Participants included in this study were part of the Prevention and Incidence of Asthma and Mite Allergy (PIAMA) population-based birth cohort established in the Netherlands in 1996.
summary: Cross-sectional analysis using quantile regression to examine associations between early-life ambient air pollution exposure and carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT) at age 16 in a Dutch birth cohort.
key_findings: PM2.5 absorbance exposure at birth was significantly associated with a 6.23 μm (95% CI: 0.15, 12.3) higher CIMT per IQR increment at the 10th quantile of CIMT.
No significant associations were found for NO2, PM2.5, PMcoarse, or ultrafine particles at other quantiles after false discovery rate correction.
PM2.5 exposure at birth was weakly associated with higher CIMT at the 10th quantile (estimate: 4.85 μm, 95% CI: −0.41, 10.10) and 20th quantile (estimate: 3.73 μm, 95% CI: −0.74, 8.20).
PMcoarse and ultrafine particles did not display any consistent patterns across CIMT deciles.
captured_features: Carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT) measured via ultrasound
Annual average air pollution concentrations (NO2, PM2.5, PM2.5 absorbance, PMcoarse, ultrafine particles)
Covariates (age, sex, BMI, cholesterol, blood pressure, parental education, indoor smoke, maternal smoking/BMI, breastfeeding, nationality)
study_design: Cross-sectional analysis within a prospective birth cohort using quantile regression
population: 363 adolescents aged 16 years from the PIAMA birth cohort in the Netherlands
exposure_domain: Ambient air pollution (NO2, PM2.5, PM2.5 absorbance, PMcoarse, ultrafine particles)
limitations: Cross-sectional design with only one CIMT measurement
Air pollution exposure estimated only at residential addresses, missing school/outdoor exposure
Findings limited to the lowest decile of CIMT distribution
